title: Trota of Salerno
summary: Trota was a healer and medical writer in 12th-century Salerno, southern Italy, one of many women there recorded as medical practitioners. She is credited with a Practica, a general manual of cures, and with the Treatments for Women text. "Trotula" is the title of a group of three texts, not a woman's name, and almost nothing is known of her life.

uncertainty.note: Green infers she lived in the early decades of the 12th century and says that is as close as we can get; the whole 12th century is used as the range.

as_recorded.value: All evidence points to the 12th century

importance.justification: The one woman of Salerno known to have a medical book credited to her, behind the much-misread Trotula tradition.
